status: WIP measurement repair and fresh comparison; no accepted Rust optimization

root_cause.source: sysbench tag 1.0.20, commit ebf1c90da05dea94648165e4f149abc20c979557; src/sb_histogram.c:115 calls ck_pr_inc_64
root_cause.cause: Bundled Concurrency Kit AArch64 inline assembly uses semicolons between instructions. The macOS ARM64 assembler treats the semicolon as a comment, dropping subsequent instructions. The installed sb_histogram_update computes the bucket address, executes mov x0,1 and returns without stadd. CK_PR_UNARY in ck_pr_lse.h constructs exactly that sequence.
root_cause.isolated_probe: clang -O2 separator.c -o separator && ./separator prints semicolon=0 newline=1
root_cause.repair: In the isolated pinned source only, replace semicolons at the ends of instruction string literals with newline escapes in gcc/aarch64/ck_pr.h, ck_pr_lse.h and ck_pr_llsc.h. Preserve the atomic instructions, constraints and barriers; do not disable atomic operations or histogram collection.
root_cause.validation: The corrected assembly contains stadd x0,[x8]. A 200-event Lua usleep(5000) probe has mean 6.11 ms in both builds; installed histogram is empty with p95 0.00, corrected histogram contains 200 events with p95 6.32 ms.
root_cause.historical_scope: Old zero percentiles are invalid. Earlier throughput and process-CPU observations retain their original executable identity and are not pooled with the corrected tool; no claim that the histogram was the only affected bundled atomic primitive.

build.notes: GNU99 is required for this source's K&R crc32 declarations with current Clang. Configure CFLAGS rather than overriding make CFLAGS, which suppresses CK's include flags. Failed setup attempts remain in build.log and build-gnu99.log; successful build-final.log and install.log are retained. Installation is exclusively under the temporary prefix. The workload Lua files match the installed oltp_read_only.lua and oltp_common.lua by diff.

comparison.method: Same owned 100000-row TiKV fixture, fixed 6000/30000/30000 read-only transactions at 1/8/32 clients; 1000-event warmup before each trial; before/after/after/before order; explicit percentile 95 and histogram enabled. Raw file includes exact commands, CPU deltas and TiKV counters.
comparison.decision: Do not accept the collector as a generic throughput-and-latency win: eight-client regression is confirmed with valid tail statistics, despite CPU savings. The 32-client direction is positive but does not override the lower-concurrency regression.
comparison.parity: Six query result sets (307 lines) match Go/control/candidate before and after; SHA256 ad1e46405a9ace48963d51a9608eb036609ada257d87fffd4943b3b79a144a4c. No errors or reconnects. Not exhaustive package or metadata parity.

runner.changes: Records min/mean/p95/max latency and median mean/p95 alongside throughput; rejects unusable zero p95; records the resolved executable and SHA256; accepts --sysbench for an isolated validated tool. Histogram quantiles are approximate, so they are not required to equal exact extrema.
runner.checks: Direct metrics() validation accepts corrected trial-1-0-before.log with p95 2.52 ms and rejects the prior trial-8-1-after.log with zero p95. git diff --check passes. No Rust production build/test or Ready lint is claimed for this measurement-only increment.

live_runner_validation.command: python3 -B rust/scripts/compare-sysbench.py --sysbench /private/tmp/tidb-latency-path.Z5pxYT/sysbench/src/sysbench --server go:57110 --server before:57112 --server after:49437 --database perf_sysbench --workload /opt/homebrew/share/sysbench/oltp_read_only.lua --threads 8 --seconds 10 --rounds 3 --table-size 100000 --output /private/tmp/tidb-latency-path.Z5pxYT/go-comparison
live_runner_validation.result: All nine runs completed without errors or reconnects. Rotating order; same corrected tool and fixture; ten seconds per trial. This is a separate window, not pooled with the fixed-work trials.
live_runner_validation.limitation: Go revision 23bff313186b8ceb61fcbe9faac43ae700e7fb14 differs from checkout HEAD. Relative results are not whole-Go-package parity or a general Rust-over-Go claim.

cleanup: Owned candidate, control, Go, TiKV and PD supervisors exited; all their ports were verified closed. Data, source, patch, binaries and logs retained. No commit or push.
remaining: Trace collection/admission/response latency against Go, then make source-backed changes that improve throughput and latency together. General prepared-plan reuse and TPC-C validation remain open.
